modern: Have I done something for the common good? Well then, I have had my reward. Let this always be present to your mind, and never stop doing such good.
original: Have I done something for the general interest? Well then, I have had my reward. Let this always be present to thy mind, and never stop [doing such good].

explained.summary: Doing something for the common good is its own reward. Marcus reminds himself that he doesn’t need thanks, recognition or a return favour to make the effort worthwhile, because the good act itself is the payoff. Keeping that in mind is what lets you carry on doing good without keeping score.
explained.today: Think of covering a shift for a colleague, clearing up after the team lunch, or helping a neighbour carry shopping in. If you’re quietly waiting for someone to notice, it sours. If the doing was the point, you’ve already been paid.
